notes.meaning: The Lord spoke to Moses and commanded him to define the boundaries of Canaan for the people of Israel. Canaan was an inheritance, meaning it was a free gift from God to His people rather than something they earned. Giving exact borders assured them of victory while also reminding them not to push into surrounding nations beyond what God provided.

The southern border ran from the southern end of the Salt Sea (the Dead Sea) westward along the edge of Edom. It passed south through Scorpion Pass and Kadesh-barnea, where Israel had once camped for years. From there it followed the Brook of Egypt, a seasonal stream, until it reached the Mediterranean Sea.

The western boundary of the land was simply the coastline of the Great Sea, known today as the Mediterranean Sea. The Bible calls it 'great' because it was vast compared to the smaller inland lakes of the region. This natural border gave Israel an open coastline along its western edge.

The northern border began at the Mediterranean Sea and ran inland toward Mount Hor in the Lebanon range. It then passed through Lebo-hamath and other northern towns until reaching Hazar-enan. This placed the northern boundary well to the north of where Israel usually lived in later generations.

The eastern border ran southward from Hazar-enan past Shepham and Riblah to the eastern hills of the Sea of Galilee. It then followed the Jordan River all the way down to the Dead Sea. This natural line kept the waters inside Israel's territory and marked off the land of Canaan proper from the region east of the river.

Moses told the people that this territory west of the Jordan was to be divided by lot among nine and a half tribes. The tribes of Reuben and Gad, along with half of Manasseh, had already received their land on the east side of the Jordan. Using lots showed that God Himself assigned each tribe its portion, helping prevent jealousy among the families.

The Lord told Moses to place Eleazar the high priest and Joshua the military commander in charge of dividing the land. God also ordered them to choose one trusted leader from each of the ten tribes receiving property. Working together, these spiritual and civil leaders ensured that the land was distributed fairly and without favoritism.

The first three leaders named were Caleb from Judah, Shemuel from Simeon, and Elidad from Benjamin. Caleb was one of the two faithful spies who had trusted God forty years earlier, and God kept His promise to bring him safely into the land. These three tribes would eventually settle together in the southern section of Canaan.

The next leaders chosen were Bukki from Dan, Hanniel from the half-tribe of Manasseh, and Kemuel from Ephraim. Manasseh and Ephraim represented the two tribes descended from Joseph. These men had the responsibility of standing up for their people and ensuring their borders were drawn properly.

The Lord then appointed Eli-zaphan from Zebulun, Paltiel from Issachar, and Ahihud from Asher. These leaders represented tribes that would settle in the northern regions of Canaan. Each man was chosen directly by God for his ability to handle this important task with fairness.

Pedahel was chosen as the leader for the tribe of Naphtali, completing the list of ten tribal heads. God named these distributors even before Israel crossed the Jordan, showing complete confidence that the land would be conquered. When the time came, these appointed men divided the country peacefully and in the presence of the Lord.
